We seek refuge in Allah from Hell and from what leads to it, namely polytheism and sins.

1. The prohibition of asking for punishment, for the punishment of Allah cannot be borne; rather, one should ask for mercy and well-being.
2. The obligation of patience in obedience and in trials, without anger or despair.
3. Affirmation of the creed of Resurrection and recompense.
4. The greatness of the horror of the Day of Resurrection and the severity of its state.
5. Condemnation of those who turn away from the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, who gather wealth and are absorbed in it, until it deprives them of faith, and Allah is our refuge, so that they come to doubt Allah, His signs, and their meeting with Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 70, verses 19–35:

Explanation of the words:

"Verily man was created impatient (halu'a)": that is, when evil touches him he is distressed (jaza'an), and when good touches him he withholds (mana'an); meaning, he is greatly prone to distress and quick to it, and greatly withholding, covetous of it.

"Constant in their prayer": that is, they never discontinue it for as long as they are living and of sound mind.

"A known right": that is, a specified portion which the Lawgiver has designated, and it is the zakat (obligatory alms).

"For the beggar and the deprived": that is, the one who asks for charity, and the one who does not ask it out of modesty and self-restraint.

"Who affirm the Day of Judgment": that is, who believe in the Day of Resurrection, for resurrection and recompense.

"Apprehensive": that is, fearful, expecting punishment when they disobey.

"Guarding their private parts": that is, preserving them from looking at them and from immorality.

"Except from their wives or those their right hands possess": that is, from the concubines (sarari) among the slave-girls whom they own.

"Then those are the transgressors (al-'adun)": that is, the aggressors, the wrongdoers, who exceed the lawful into the unlawful.

"[Who are] faithful to their trusts": that is, what they have been entrusted with of matters of religion and worldly affairs.

"Maintainers (ra'un)": that is, guarding them, without negligence.

"Upright (qa'imun)": that is, they uphold their testimonies, neither concealing them nor distorting them.

"Who maintain": that is, they perform them at their appointed times, in congregation, with all the conditions, pillars, obligations and recommended practices.

Explanation of the meaning of the verses:

The statement of the Exalted: "Verily man", that is, this human being, upright of stature, laughing, who is named "insan" (human) because of his affection for himself and his seeing its beauties, and because of his forgetfulness of the duty of thanking his Lord: "was created impatient", meaning he is inclined to the characteristic of impatience (al-hal') when he reaches the age of discernment. Al-hal' is a psychological illness whose symptom by which it is known is extreme distress when evil touches him, and strong withholding of good when it touches him and he attains it. The Exalted explained impatience by His saying: "When evil touches him, he is distressed; and when good touches him, he withholds." Then the Exalted mentioned what this illness is treated with, by excepting from the human species those who are characterized by the following attributes, which are acts of worship prescribed by the Law, some of them actions and some abstentions, which are capable of eliminating this dangerous illness called impatience, which is treated only by what the Exalted described in His saying:

1) Persistence in prayer through constancy in it, night and day, as the Exalted said: "Except those who pray, who are constant in their prayer," on condition that it is performed in faith and seeking reward, and performed correctly, observing its conditions, pillars and recommended practices.

2) Acknowledging the right that God has obligated in wealth, and giving that right willingly to the one who asks and to the one who does not ask, of those who are deserving of zakat and charity, by His saying: "And those in whose wealth there is a known right, for the beggar and the deprived."

That is the mockery they direct at you, and they say, in ridicule of the believers: "If these people enter the Garden, we will surely enter it before them."

And His words, ﴿ذَلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلَّذِي كانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ﴾, i.e., this is the day on which they were promised punishment, the Day of Resurrection, which they denied and rejected. Here it has come to pass, so let them now drink the bitter draughts of regret and every kind of punishment.

2. A demonstration that entry into the Garden is through spiritual purity from the filth of polytheism and sins. Otherwise, the origin of all people is one: foul semen, with the exception of Adam, Eve and Jesus. Adam's origin was clay; Eve was created from Adam's rib; and Jesus came through the breathing of the Holy Spirit into the garment of Mary, so he came by the word of Allah, the Exalted. Apart from these three, all others come from a despicable fluid and a foul drop.

3. Reasoning from the first creation to the possibility of the second.

4. Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

5. A demonstration that the life of the disbelievers, however it appears to them and to others as a happy worldly life, is nothing but falsehood, idle play and amusement.
